corrections.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins confronts Folley’s regulative-fiction alternative, interpreting Bradley’s normative orientation toward consummated truth as ontological commitment relevant to the central realism burden. Principal limitation: The inference equivocates between evaluative superiority and metaphysical actuality: recognizing comprehensive understanding as normatively authoritative neither demonstrates an independently existent completion nor necessitates an already-real terminus. Live burden: Hawkins must justify why truth-directed aspiration metaphysically presupposes a completed whole, excluding the charitable possibility that regulative ideals guide indefinitely improvable inquiry without corresponding to any separately existing absolute. Locked score: The mixed 65–74 band appropriately recognizes direct, fully responsive burden contact and a recoverable Bradley-specific rationale, while substantially discounting materially overstated necessity, unstable “more real” terminology, unacknowledged modal uncertainty, and comparatively weak ontological warrant.
